Title: May 14, 2026 Boulder City Council Study Session: Financial Forecast and 2026 Ballot Measures

Topic1.Title: Economic Conditions and Financial Forecast Presentation
Topic1.Summary: CU Boulder's Business Research Division presented economic conditions affecting Boulder sales and use tax, noting modest GDP growth, stalled national employment, Colorado job losses, and rising inflation driven by energy prices. Staff explained that sales and use tax and property tax revenues are flattening and forecasts were lowered for 2026 and 2027. Council members asked about recession risk, federal policy impacts, and the Federal Reserve's stance. The forecast uses a medium economic scenario with statistical bounds.

Topic2.Title: 2026 and 2027 Budget Shortfalls and Department Reductions
Topic2.Summary: Staff reported that 2025 required a hiring freeze and 5% operating savings to close an 8 to 10 million shortfall, and 2026 required a 7.8% general fund reduction. A $6.5 million general fund shortfall for 2027 prompts requested 4% reductions across departments. The care program was restructured into a cross-functional behavioral health team. Council asked for more transparency on how reductions affect services and the public.

Topic3.Title: Sales and Property Tax Revenue Forecasts
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented sales and use tax actuals and forecasts showing retail sales tax flattening at around 1% annual growth and a forecasted decline in 2026. Property tax projections were revised down by about 7 million due to state legislation and lack of growth, with reassessment growth at only 0.2%. Council asked about the sales to property tax ratio and the impact of Sundance revenue, which will be cautiously incorporated in year one.

Topic4.Title: 2027 Budget Calendar and Process
Topic4.Summary: Staff outlined the 2027 budget timeline: department submissions in mid-June, executive budget team decisions in July, city manager's recommended budget on August 28, a study session on September 10, and first and second readings on October 1 and 15. Council discussed how to provide input and the desire for a two-year budget cycle. Council also asked for budget-versus-actual data at the project level.

Topic5.Title: Long-Term Financial Strategy and Ballot Measure Framework
Topic5.Summary: Staff described the long-term financial strategy, including a comprehensive financial plan due in late 2026, and explained that about 68% of city revenue is already committed to specific purposes. General fund expenses have grown faster than revenue. Staff noted that polling works best with three to four items and that ballot measures should be sequenced with other measures. Council discussed the need to communicate trade-offs clearly to the public.

Topic6.Title: Facilities Investment Needs and Funding Scenarios
Topic6.Summary: Staff reported that 15 priority city buildings, including recreation centers and the public safety building, need about 20 million over five to six years for critical maintenance and roughly 400 million in unfunded priority needs. Five funding scenarios were presented, mixing existing CCRS tax authority, a parks and public improvement mill levy, general obligation debt, and a charter change to the 3% debt limit. Staff recommended scenarios C and E, providing up to 200 million. Council discussed impacts on residents and businesses and the need for polling on specific projects and thresholds.

Topic7.Title: Council Direction on Ballot Measure Polling
Topic7.Summary: Council gave direction to poll on the parks and public improvement mill levy expansion, a 200 million general obligation debt authorization with associated mill levy, and a charter change to the debt limit. Council members expressed mixed views on including the 400 million option, the general fund debt authorization, and the flexibility of language. Staff will bring polling results in late June and return with ballot ordinances in summer.

Topic8.Title: Residential Vacancy Excise Tax Discussion
Topic8.Summary: Staff sought direction on whether to pursue a residential vacancy excise tax, a second homes tax applied to properties vacant at least 183 days. Council members discussed tiered structures based on square footage, higher maximum amounts, whether to use an ordinance rather than a ballot initiative for flexibility, and legal research on the approach. Council members supported further analysis and polling, with some expressing concerns about housing impacts.

Topic9.Title: Charter Amendments: Boards and Commissions and Open Space Wildfire Mitigation
Topic9.Summary: The charter committee recommended revisiting a boards and commissions amendment from 2024, which failed, and adding wildfire mitigation as an explicit purpose of open space under charter section 176. Council discussed removing removal provisions, adding flood mitigation, and the timing of these changes. Council decided not to move boards and commissions forward this year but directed staff to continue research on the wildfire open space amendment.

Topic10.Title: Community Petitions and State and Regional Ballot Measures
Topic10.Summary: Staff noted one community-sponsored petition on commercial and residential vacancy taxes and provided information on potential state of Colorado ballot measures with tax impacts. Boulder County and Boulder Valley School District ballot measures are yet to be determined. A legislative update is planned for June. A council member requested a future meeting to take positions on several potential ballot measures.
